'''''Jaecheop-guk''''' ({{Korean|hangul=재첩국}}) is a clear ''[[guk]]'' (soup) made with [[Corbicula leana|''jaecheop'']], small [[freshwater]] [[Corbicula|marsh clams]] native to Korea.<ref name="Kohler">{{Cite iucn|last=Köhler|first=F.|date=2011|title=Corbicula leana|doi=10.2305/iucn.uk.2011-2.rlts.t189564a8748990.en}}</ref> The soup is considered a local specialty of [[Yeongnam]] and [[Honam]] regions, where ''jaecheop'' are harvested in the lower reaches of [[Nakdong River]] and [[Seomjin River]].<ref name="Lee">{{Cite news|url=http://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/news/article/article.aspx?aid=2914219|title=Healthy, hearty hangover soup|last=Lee|first=Sang-eun|date=19 December 2009|work=[[Korea JoongAng Daily]]}}</ref><ref name="Koehler">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dF6tCQAAQBAJ&pg=PT101|title=Traditional Food: A Taste of Korean Life|last=Koehler|first=Robert|publisher=Seoul Selection|year=2012|isbn=978-1-62412-036-7|location=Seoul|pages=101}}</ref>

Chopped [[Allium tuberosum|garlic chives]] or [[Allium fistulosum|scallions]] along with minced [[garlic]] is typically added at the end of the cooking process.<ref name="Doo">{{Cite web|url=http://www.doopedia.co.kr/doopedia/master/master.do?_method=view&MAS_IDX=101013000796828|title=jaecheop-guk|website=[[Doopedia]]|publisher=[[Doosan Corporation]]|script-title=ko:재첩국|access-date=8 April 2017}}</ref> The soup is usually seasoned with salt and eaten as a [[Haejang-guk|hangover soup]]. It is also available as a packaged product.
